explanation: The statement is about the library's own definition `Submodule.diagBlock` (`P A P + P_{Uᗮ} A P_{Uᗮ}`); a grep for `diagBlock`/`offDiagBlock` and similar block-decomposition names over the whole Mathlib tree returns nothing, so no Mathlib declaration states this result. I also checked the plausible general-ring candidates: `IsIdempotentElem.{one_sub, mul_one_sub_self, one_sub_mul_self, add_sub_mul}` in Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/Idempotent.lean, `LinearMap.IsIdempotentElem.*` (LinearAlgebra/Projection.lean) and `ContinuousLinearMap.IsIdempotentElem.commute_iff` (Topology/Algebra/Module/ContinuousLinearMap/Idempotent.lean) — none of them talks about `p * a * p + (1 - p) * a * (1 - p)` commuting with `p`, so nothing gives the claim by instantiation. Any derivation would have to unfold `diagBlock`, rewrite `Uᗮ.starProjection` to `1 - U.starProjection` via `Submodule.starProjection_orthogonal'` and then do a nontrivial computation in the endomorphism ring, which is well beyond one or two glue lines. Note only that the ingredients used in the proof (`Submodule.starProjection_orthogonal'`, `Submodule.isIdempotentElem_starProjection`) are Mathlib lemmas, but they do not carry the theorem's content.
